title: SuperTruck 2: Empowering Future Trucking
abstract: This video summary reviews the outcomes of the Department of Energy's SuperTruck 2 initiative, evaluated in a NACFE report. Five OEM teams—Cummins/Peterbilt, Daimler, Navistar, Volvo, and PACCAR—exceeded the project's goal of a 100% freight ton efficiency improvement over 2009 baselines, achieving overall improvements up to 134% and fuel economy of 14–16 MPG. Key advancements highlighted include 51–55% engine brake thermal efficiency, aggressive lightweighting, optimized aerodynamics, mild-hybridization, and driver-focused cab designs tested in real-world operating conditions.
key_findings: All five OEM teams significantly exceeded the goal of a 100% freight ton efficiency improvement over Model Year 2009 baselines.
Demonstrated Class 8 truck fuel economy of 14 to 16 miles per gallon carrying representative payloads in real-world driving conditions.
Engine development achieved 51% to 55% brake thermal efficiency (BTE), supporting requirements for 2027 Phase 3 Greenhouse Gas regulations.
Efficiency gains were driven by lightweighting, optimized aerodynamics, 4x2 axle configurations, central drive positioning, and mild-hybrid electrification.
